title: Strata reserve bands + SmartBurst pricing playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Enterprise prospects repeatedly ask for predictable committed GPU pricing, granular burst mechanics, and clear autoscale/overage rules tied to SLAs. Previous pilots (various slab/surge and tokenized overage experiments) surfaced trade-offs: simple buckets are easy to sell but inefficient for mixed workloads; unlimited burst promises are risky without throttles or dynamic pricing; and autoscale needs deterministic billing paths for contracts.

Objective: Produce a playbook outlining (1) a stratified reserve band model (Strata bands) that maps commit tiers to capacity guarantees and priority bursting; (2) SmartBurst operational and billing mechanics with deterministic throttles and dispute resolution; and (3) autoscale/overage rules that integrate with SLA tiers and contract language. Deliverables: narrative playbook, quote templates, sample contract clauses for burst and overage, customer FAQ, pricing simulations, and a go/no-go rollout checklist.

Success metrics: (a) 25% reduction in commercial negotiation time for dedicated deals; (b) 10% higher attach rate for burst add-ons on new Dedicated contracts; (c) <2% incidence of billing disputes during first 3 months of rollout; (d) measurable unit-economics uplift (cost-per-token) vs current committed-only baseline.

Scope & non-goals: Focus on reserved GPU-based Dedicated product (not hosted API). Do not redesign low-level autoscaling engine — align on existing autoscale primitives from ENG. Excludes vertical-specific compliance deviations (handled by Private product team).

Approach:
1) Define Strata reserve bands: three primary bands (Core, Surge, Peak) with example numeric buckets (e.g., 4-GPU, 16-GPU, 64-GPU equivalents) and corresponding throughput SLAs. Each band includes: guaranteed GPU-minutes, burst credits allocation, and priority routing weight.
2) SmartBurst mechanics: implement credit-based bursting where committed customers accumulate burst credits on steady-state underutilization; credits redeem for short bursts above guaranteed throughput up to a cap; define hard throttles and graceful degradation policies; specify how fallback to compatible model variants occurs during sustained overutilization.
3) Autoscale & overage rules: autoscale triggers mapped to customer-configurable policies (aggressive, conservative); overage billed at a transparent, pre-agreed rate with a monthly cap; include an automatic credit reconciliation window and an escalation path to customer success for disputes.
4) SLA tier alignment: link Strata bands to SLA tiers (latency p95, availability, throughput) and define remedy table (credits, service credits, or manual remediation steps).
5) Commercial artifacts: pricing calculator spreadsheets, quote templates with line-item burst credits, legal-friendly clauses for burst/overage, and a short sales play one-pager.

Pricing experiments matrix (planned):
- Fixed-band pricing: flat monthly fee for a Strata band + included burst credit pool.
- Pay-as-you-burst: lower base commit price + per-GPU-minute burst rate with monthly cap.
- Hybrid: higher commit + discounted burst rates + rollover of unused burst credits.
Run A/B experiments across 3 pilot customers per segment (AI startup, mid-market SaaS, enterprise regulated) to collect elasticity and acceptance signals.

Contract considerations: clear definitions ("burst event", "burst credit", "overage window"), billing cadence, audit logs access for customers, and termination/transition language when downgrading bands. Legal to review indemnity and SLA remedy language—include mandatory escalation SLA for billing disputes (72 hours initial response, 10 business-day resolution window).

Operational requirements: integrate playbook with Billing (line-item for burst credits), Console (dashboard showing burst credit balance and forecasted exhaustion), and Runtime (enforcement of throttles; telemetry for disputed events). Engineering dependencies documented in dependencies. Ensure observability hooks for latency-by-route during bursts.

Stakeholders: Sales (quote/negotiation), Legal (contract language), Billing/Finance (invoicing & GL), Engineering (autoscale & enforcement), Console/UX (dashboard), Customer Success (onboarding & disputes).

Risks & mitigations:
- Excessive tail-costs if burst pricing is too generous — mitigate by caps and dynamic throttles.
- Customer confusion — mitigate with clear one-pagers, demo dashboards, and sales enablement training.
- Engineering enforcement complexity — mitigate by constraining initial SmartBurst to engineered-safe primitives and phased rollout.

Open questions:
- Optimal expiry window for accumulated burst credits (monthly vs rolling 90 days)?
- Should burst credits be transferrable across subaccounts under an enterprise org?
- What is the acceptable financial liability cap for sales to sign without additional legal review?

Next steps (immediate):
- 2025-03-05: Workshop with Sales + Finance to agree on 3 pilot price points.
- 2025-03-10: Legal draft of required contract clauses.
- 2025-03-17: Instrument Console mock showing burst balance.
- 2025-03-28: Selection of pilot customers and execute pilot NDA or addendum.

2025-03-09: Legal flagged two clauses needing negotiation: liability cap for burst overage and audit scope for customer access to logs. Action: schedule legal deep-dive on 2025-03-10.
